answer: A sybil attacker must fund many independent stakes plus sustain costly work to build standing, while honest participants share an oasis of low-fee attestations. Each agent must stake a bond at the wharf registry before voting, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations over multiple epochs. Colluding clusters are pruned when their graph overlaps tightly, like a grove cut back to healthy roots, so the attack cost scales with identity count rather than one wallet. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
